quote: Are you are you, like, a subcontractor of Tesla?
stewart_read: First direct legitimacy check tied to the Tesla lead source; rep's 'preferred installer' answer is accurate but incomplete, leaving the product-mix confusion alive.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep answered honestly and moved on because he genuinely didn't anticipate the follow-up about free roofs. Strategic read: rejected — nothing in the transcript shows deliberate sequencing, the rep is visibly improvising each subsequent answer.
coaching_implication: Should have proactively clarified Ion sells its own panels + Powerwall, not Tesla roof product, before the customer had to ask twice more.

quote: I was under the understanding that Tesla was offering, like, free free solar roofs with, battery.
stewart_read: Second touch on the same expectation gap; rep denies knowledge instead of reframing the referral relationship cleanly.
coaching_implication: This was the moment for the scripted reframe line about Tesla being a lead source, not a product line — rep had it available and didn't use it.

quote: now it just sounds like you're just a solar company trying to sell sell me solar.
stewart_read: Third and final touch; customer names the bait-and-switch feeling directly and the rep's response trails off without resolution.
coaching_implication: By the third occurrence this is a lost legitimacy battle — the call needed the clean reframe at touch one, not left to compound.

quote: I'm I'm scheduled to get a new roof with a fifty year warranty.
stewart_read: Textbook roof-replacement cross-sell trigger; rep says 'Oh, nice' and stays on the solar-durability tangent instead of bridging to Ion's in-house roofing team.
coaching_implication: Should have pivoted immediately: Ion does roofing in-house, offer to route to that team for both the roof job and a future solar sale.

quote: definitely can't, like, think about solar until I get a new roof.
stewart_read: Second touch on the same roofing signal; rep concedes and tells the customer to call back later, walking away from both the roofing sale and the future solar lead.
coaching_implication: This is the negative example the schema explicitly calls out (Jake/Larry) — the correct move was bridging to roofing team, not deferring to a callback.

quote: in a traditional solar system, kind of the way it goes with one inverter is if one panel start like, it doesn't work, your whole system is broken.
stewart_read: Rep gets pulled into a detailed micro-inverter design debate with a self-identified electronics-literate customer, ground he cannot win and shouldn't be defending.
coaching_implication: Escape hatch was available and named earlier by the rep himself — should have redirected to the specialist instead of debating failure-point counts.

quote: y'all bought my information from some other company. Right?
stewart_read: Trust/scam-adjacent objection about data sourcing; rep confirms the practice plainly instead of reframing toward the customer's own control (they filled out a form) or pivoting to value.
coaching_implication: A cleaner move acknowledges the form submission specifically (protocols.how_did_you_get_my_number) rather than confirming resale to 'a few companies,' which deepens the scam perception.

quote: I think I have to have more trees taken down
stewart_read: Customer volunteers tree removal already in progress, a strong solar-readiness signal (more sun exposure coming).
coaching_implication: Rep acknowledged it functionally (adjusted the satellite image note) but never used it as a forward-pulling hook to build urgency toward booking.
